sources.entry: TouchGrassBar - Shows Codex and Claude limits, observed token usage, trends, and public friend rankings from the macOS menu bar.

summary.one_liner: TouchGrassBar is a macOS menu-bar app (built with Tauri and React) that shows Codex and Claude usage limits, locally observed token activity, and public Token Score rankings on a "Doomerboard."
keywords: see how much claude i use
summary.what_it_does: TouchGrassBar is a macOS menu-bar app for checking Codex and Claude limits. It shows locally observed token activity and trends. It also lets users compare public Token Scores on the Doomerboard, including public friend rankings. The repository is a monorepo with a Tauri/React desktop app, an Astro landing site, a Convex backend package, shared contracts and UI packages, and shared TypeScript tooling. The README describes the project as an open, playful consumer app and explicitly not an employee-monitoring or productivity product. Setup and dev commands are run with Bun, and the desktop app is built as a signed native bundle.
use_cases: check Codex and Claude usage limits from the menu bar
track local token usage for AI coding tools
compare public Token Scores with friends
view usage trends over time on macOS
develop or contribute to a Tauri and Convex monorepo
how_to_run: Install Bun, the stable Rust toolchain, and the macOS prerequisites for Tauri
bun desktop:bundle (builds a signed development app bundle)
notable: Uses an anonymous local Convex deployment on first setup, with no Convex account required
Per-worktree development labels and isolated runtime namespaces
Reset and clean commands with explicit data boundaries that preserve remote and production state
Release workflow with Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, notarization, and stapling
caveats: Requires macOS and the Tauri macOS prerequisites, plus Bun and the stable Rust toolchain
Development signing relies on a configured development provisioning profile for Keychain access
Cloud deployment and production release steps require explicit credentials and authority
